A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RCORE study, with matching authors, research question, and benchmark foundations. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original controlled shortcut-learning experiments, Sth-com and EK100-com evaluations, and diagnostic and ablation results in the main text and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, controlled experiments, revised ablations, and additional backbone, error-decomposition, and macro-compositional-gap results.

M1.justification: V2 substantially reworks VOCAMix and the margin loss into CPR. It retains motion-preserving object mixing but introduces explicit synthesized-composition targets, batch-adaptive training-label expansion, and penalties against frequent shared-component hard negatives instead of v1's top-K penalties relative to the original target. It also adapts InternVideo2 pooling for frame-level features. TORC's cosine and entropy objectives remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use Sth-com and EK100-com, the same controlled 10-by-10 and biased 4-by-4 subsets, and the same original and reconstructed Temporal/Static scenarios. Dataset construction and reported split counts are retained. Added backbones and metrics do not expand data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator suite loses several distinct controls: C2C without conditioning disappears from the Sth-com comparisons, CutMix disappears from augmentation comparisons, and L-softmax disappears from margin-loss comparisons. V2 adds independently trained InternVideo2+LoRA comparison rows. C2C, AIM, Jung et al., and Mixup remain in their relevant comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported CLIP training increases from 30 to 40 epochs; new InternVideo2 configurations use eight-frame inputs and 40–50 epochs. Augmentation and loss schedules change substantially. V2 specifies primitive accuracies from joint top-1 composition predictions instead of v1's separate component logits, revises FCP normalization, and adds macro-CG evaluation. These are reported setting changes, not proof that every retained result was rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds verb/object/dual-collapse analyses, macro-CG checks for class imbalance, CPR label-space and penalty-set ablations, and backbone-size analysis. It removes v1's confidence-distribution study and top-K margin sweep. Random-initialization, temporal-reversal, failure-case, and Temporal/Static analyses remain, with several relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both report point estimates and learning curves; frequency-distribution statistics are not experimental uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Reported unbiased CLIP RCORE composition results change substantially: Sth-com seen/unseen/H.M. changes from 48.56/32.23/38.75 to 44.99/33.90/38.67, and EK100-com from 43.86/24.24/31.23 to 39.70/28.41/33.12. Closed-world Sth-com H.M./AUC changes from 45.45/26.52 to 43.21/25.27. InternVideo2, 1B-backbone, and macro-CG entries are added, while calibrated EK100-com entries disappear. Changed methods and settings prevent treating these replacements as controlled version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Formal definitions change substantially. V1 Appendix B.1 normalizes FCP by false-seen predictions; v2 Appendix C.1 uses all unseen samples. V2 changes CG's component-prediction basis and introduces classwise macro-CG and component-collapse definitions. CPR also introduces new hard-negative and expanded-label-space formulations. V2's main-text normalization descriptions remain inconsistent with its appendix equations.

C1.justification: The central shortcut diagnosis remains, but the methodological contribution is redefined around CPR's synthesized supervision and hard-negative regularization plus TORC. V2 extends its principal effectiveness claim to multiple VLM backbones. The abstract's earlier assertion of consistently positive compositional gaps is dropped, and the diagnosis is framed as a key failure mode rather than the primary explanation for failure.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies CG as a supporting diagnostic rather than a standalone criterion, explicitly discusses seen–unseen performance trade-offs, and explains why full-space training can suppress unseen classes. It adds interpretations concerning persistent shortcuts after video pretraining and zero optimal calibration bias, plus a substantive rationale for restricting the study to encoder-based VLM interfaces.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds InternVideo2 adaptation and frame-level pooling details, backbone-specific input lengths and hyperparameters, and model-selection information. Training schedules, augmentation strengths, and margin parameters are revised or expanded relative to v1 Appendix B.2. V2 also removes v1's explicit code-availability statement and repository link; this does not establish that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands its CAR, open-vocabulary, and encoder-versus-decoder VLM positioning, adding discussions of InternVideo2, LoRA, LLaVA, Qwen-VL, and other compositional approaches. V2 acknowledges earlier object/static-cue debiasing work and replaces v1's categorical novelty and image-CZSL distinctions with a more specific account of sparse supervision and temporal grounding.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, related work, method description, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. V2 adds a separate training subsection and an evaluation-protocol appendix, reorganizes supplementary analyses, and consistently reframes the method around CPR.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting, redraws the conceptual and method diagrams, expands Figure 3 with backbone comparisons and error-breakdown charts, and adds evaluation diagrams in Figures 7–8. Results tables are separated and reorganized across evaluation settings. Random-initialization and reversal-similarity plots move to the appendix.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens evidence beyond v1's CLIP-focused evaluation through InternVideo2 and 1B-backbone comparisons, while CPR ablations and macro-CG analysis make methodological and class-imbalance claims more testable. Its more cautious interpretation of CG also improves the argument. These benefits are tempered by conflicting diagnostic definitions between Section 3.2 and Appendix C.1, inconsistent updated figure annotations, and removal of several comparison controls and the code link. The net improvement is limited despite the substantial revision.
